**Continuous 2.38.5**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.38.4, 2.38.3, 2.38.2, 2.38.1, 2.38.0, 2.36.0, 2.34.0, 2.32.0, 2.30.0, 2.28.0, 2.26.0, 2.24.0, 2.22.0, 2.20.0, 2.18.0, 2.16.3, 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.38.5.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.38.5.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.38.5.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.38.5.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.38.5.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.38.5.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.38.5.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.38.5-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.38.5.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.38.5-vscode/continuous-cli-2.38.5.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.38.4

Safety checks are separate switches, and a preset sets them. IDGAF leaves every check off until you turn one on. The terminal tool can name a working directory, and the audit records how a command ended. Folders you list in your own config count as the workspace for the outside-paths check. A decision timer can count down before a decision takes effect, and it is off until you set a window. Files the agent creates or edits are shown without taking the keyboard. A subagent may make 50 model calls by default.

No new host is contacted by the extension or the terminal agent.

### New

- **Safety checks.** Each check is its own switch on the shield and under Settings > Tools. Careful, Accept edits, Hands off, Reviewer and IDGAF set which ones are on. IDGAF sets none. A check you turn back on stays on. An old `safetyChecks: off` line is read as every check off.
- **Working directory.** The terminal tool takes a `cwd` inside the workspace. The permission check reads that folder. A folder outside the workspace is still reached with `cd` in the command, and the path checks judge it as before.
- **Wait.** Waiting for a background command waits until it ends.
- **Added folders.** List folders in your own `config.yaml` under `toolPermissions.auto.environment.additionalFolders`. A listed folder counts as the workspace for the outside-paths check only, in the editor and in the CLI. Secret files, files that change what runs later, and the locked policy files still ask inside it. A link that leaves it still asks. A workspace file cannot set the list.
- **Decision timer.** A short countdown shows what the policy already decided and lets you answer differently. An ask shows "Refused in 12 s unless you answer", with Keep waiting. If nobody answers, it is refused. An allowed call can show "Runs in 5 s unless you answer". Reject stops it, Accept runs it now, and if nobody answers it runs. Set a window per level on the Approval card, or with `levels.timer` and `levels.headsUp` in `permissions.yaml`. Both are off until you set them. Asks use 5, 10, 15 or 30 seconds. Allowed calls use 5 or 10. A refusal from a rule you wrote, a floor, a guard, or anything at IDGAF never gets a countdown. The terminal agent shows the same countdown on an ask (`w` keeps waiting). It does not hold allowed calls, and it holds nothing in `cn serve`, the editor link, or a headless run.

### Behaviour changes

- **IDGAF.** Every safety check is off. A tool you switched off stays off. A write to a locked policy file runs, and the audit says the rule would have refused it. The checks that are not switches, including the ones on web fetches, still apply.
- **Permissive.** Its glyph is a play triangle. The text says what a rule does not decide.
- **Focus.** A file the agent creates or edits is shown without moving the keyboard into it. A link in the chat, and Open the plan file, still take focus.
- **Subagents.** The default limit is 50 model calls, up from 30. A definition's own `maxTurns` still wins. At the limit the run stops and writes its report.

### Fixes

- **Highlighted code.** Ctrl+L (Cmd+L on macOS) with text selected adds that code to a new chat.
- **PWD.** Printing the working directory is not treated as printing a password. `DB_PWD`, `MYSQL_PWD` and `PWD_FILE` still ask.
- **Credential stores.** More home folders and files that hold credentials ask, including browser profiles, Windows credential folders, and the credential files common tools write. Commands that print or send a credential without naming a secret file ask too.
- **Windows paths.** An absolute path that names a file inside the open workspace is found there. On Windows, folder names are compared without regard to case. A path outside the workspace still asks.
